examples.title: One resource, every status
examples.code:
GET    /api/tasks?done=false&page=2   → 200 OK, one page of the list
GET    /api/tasks/42                  → 200 OK, or 404 Not Found
POST   /api/tasks  {"title":"…"}      → 201 Created, Location: /api/tasks/43
POST   /api/tasks  {"title":""}       → 400 Bad Request, {"error":"Enter a title"}
PATCH  /api/tasks/42  {"done":true}   → 200 OK, the updated task
DELETE /api/tasks/42                  → 204 No Content
DELETE /api/tasks                     → 405 Method Not Allowed, Allow: GET, POST
GET    /api/projects/7/tasks          → 200 OK, the tasks of project 7
examples.takeaway: The URL names the thing and the method says what to do with it; the status tells the client how it went before it reads a byte of the body.

examples.title: Constraints do the checking
examples.code:
CREATE TABLE users (
  id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  email text NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (email = lower(email)),
  name text NOT NULL CHECK (length(name) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES ('asha@example.com', 'Asha');  -- OK
INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES ('asha@example.com', 'Sam');   -- ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "users_email_key"
INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES ('Sam@Example.com', 'Sam');    -- ERROR: new row for relation "users" violates check constraint "users_email_check"
INSERT INTO users (email) VALUES ('sam@example.com');                  -- ERROR: null value in column "name" of relation "users" violates not-null constraint

-- Taken or not, in one statement that no race can break: no row back means the email was taken.
INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES ('asha@example.com', 'Asha again')
ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING
RETURNING id;
examples.takeaway: Every write, from every part of the code, meets the same rules; and `ON CONFLICT` answers “is it taken?” in one statement no race can break.
